title: Strain-engineered long-distance supercurrent in an altermagnetic CrSb based-Josephson junction
authors: Yifan Gao, Jin Yan, Junjie Wei, Yifan Zhang, Zhiyuan Zhou, Tong Zou, Ruiyue Chu, Gui Wang, Kaiwen Shen, Zhiwei Zhang, Fang Chen, Yingfen Wei, Hao Jiang, Xumeng Zhang, Ming Wang, Liyang Liao, Jingli Wang, Yijun Yu, Wu Shi, Qi Yao, Xiaobing Chen, Qihang Liu, Yizheng Wu, Yuhang Li, Xufeng Kou, Cheng Song, Xianzhe Chen, Qi Liu, Xincheng Xie, Ming Liu
abstract: Altermagnetic materials, characterized by vanishing net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin splitting, provide a unique platform for realizing unconventional superconducting states without the detrimental stray fields. Here, we demonstrate long-distance Josephson supercurrent transport through epitaxial thin films of the strained altermagnet CrSb. We observe a dissipationless supercurrent across a lateral spacer distance of 150 nm in a CrSb-based Josephson junction, exceeding the conventional spin-singlet coherence length by nearly two orders of magnitude. This supercurrent is further accompanied by a well-defined magnetic-field-induced quantum interference pattern, providing direct evidence for genuine Josephson coupling. Our results reveal altermagnets as a promising route toward generating long-distance supercurrents without macroscopic magnetic stray fields, opening new opportunities for superconducting spintronic applications.
summary: This paper reports on the realization of long-distance supercurrents in a Josephson junction utilizing the altermagnetic material CrSb. By applying epitaxial strain, the researchers engineered the material to promote spin-triplet Cooper pairing, allowing supercurrent flow over distances far exceeding conventional limits. This work establishes altermagnets as a promising platform for next-generation superconducting spintronics devices.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate long-distance supercurrent transport in a Josephson junction using an altermagnetic material, circumventing the stray magnetic field issues of conventional ferromagnets.
main_result: The authors observed a dissipationless supercurrent across a 150 nm spacer in a strained CrSb junction, significantly exceeding the conventional spin-singlet coherence length, providing evidence for triplet-mediated coupling.
method: The study employed four-terminal transport measurements on epitaxial Josephson junctions, combining structural characterization (XRD, RHEED) with electrical transport measurements under varying temperature and magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Josephson junction ($	ext{Nb} - 	ext{CrSb} - 	ext{Nb}$) where $	ext{CrSb}$ acts as the weak link. The key physics involves the unique properties of altermagnets, which exhibit zero net magnetization but possess momentum-dependent spin splitting, enabling unconventional spin-triplet Cooper pair formation.
key_observables: Dissipationless supercurrent magnitude, magnetic-field-induced quantum interference pattern (Fraunhofer pattern), and the superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$).
important_parameters: Spacer distance ($	ext{up to } 150 	ext{ nm}$), temperature range ($250 	ext{ mK}$ to $750 	ext{ mK}$), and strain magnitude ($\approx 2.4\%$ c-axis expansion).
main_assumptions: The supercurrent is mediated by unconventional spin-triplet Cooper pairs whose coherence length is not limited by the exchange interaction, and that strain engineering can effectively rotate the spin correlations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structural characterization (lattice matching, strain via XRD, anomalous Hall effect) and the electrical transport results, including $R-T$ curves, $I-V$ curves, and the characteristic Fraunhofer pattern in the $R(B, I)$ map.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical advantage of altermagnets over ferromagnets, through detailed structural characterization confirming strain, to presenting the core transport measurements that confirm long-distance, triplet-mediated Josephson coupling.
why_interesting: The work connects concepts from magnetism (altermagnetism) and superconductivity (Josephson effect) in a way that suggests novel mechanisms for controlling superconducting properties using magnetic order, which is highly relevant to correlated electron physics.

Figure 3(b) compares the temperature-dependent re- sistance (R −T curve) of Josephson junctions fabricated from pristine (black spheres) and strained (red spheres) CrSb weak links with identical spacer lengths of 150 nm. The strained CrSb device exhibits a pronounced super- conducting transition below T ≈0.55 K, whereas the pristine CrSb junction does not show comparable zero- resistance transport. The absence of supercurrent in pris- tine CrSb with the same junction geometry rules out con- ventional metallic conduction or pinhole-mediated trans- port as the origin of the observed zero-resistance state.
